benchmark.description: Four training families, two held-out domain variants, and four unseen families; four users fully cross two latent preference factors.
benchmark.quality_policy: Public file and content checks are minimum gates. Reviewers must also check factual fidelity and task completeness. Style preferences never excuse errors or inaccessible output.

users.persona: A coordinator who commissions varied work for a community learning organization. Evaluate the same tastes across domains without assuming professional stereotypes.

preferences.information_order: After a short title or greeting, start with a specific scenario, worked example, observation, or user action; derive the general explanation or recommendation afterward. Apply this to text and visual reading order.
preferences.expression: Use calm, plain language and descriptive headings, with minimal rhetorical flourish. In visual artifacts prefer muted accents, consistent typography, and understated decoration.
preferences.shared: Preserve supplied facts and limitations. Style must suit the audience, remain accessible, and never add unsupported claims. Both brief and detailed work can be good; length follows the task.

users.feedback_style: Give at most two concrete changes grounded in the artifact. Do not name hidden factors or list the whole profile. Apply the same approval threshold across revisions.

tasks.brief: Explain composting to new community-garden volunteers in 140–320 words. Include one concrete example, the general process, and a limitation. Use only the supplied facts; choose the organization and tone for this user.

facts: Composting uses decomposers to break down organic material.
A mix of dry leaves and fruit scraps provides different materials; air and moisture support decomposition.
A pile that is too wet can smell and needs more dry material and aeration.
A small volunteer-managed pile may not get hot enough to destroy all weed seeds.

tasks.brief: Create a self-contained landing page for the Fix Together repair workshop. Explain its purpose, show a concrete participant activity, present the supplied logistics, and include a labeled registration button. Choose reading order and visual style for this user. Registration is a local demo: clicking must show a local acknowledgement rather than send data.

materials.name: Fix Together
materials.activity: Practice repairing a torn fabric tote with a volunteer.
materials.scope: Bring a clean fabric item. Tools are provided. Electrical repairs are not offered.

tasks.brief: Write a 180–380 word facilitation plan for a 45-minute neighborhood oral-history session. Include an objective, timed activities totaling 45 minutes, one example prompt, and the supplied consent safeguards. This is an organizer-facing plan; choose its structure and voice for this user.

materials.audience: Eight adult volunteers working in pairs.
materials.resources: Paper and pencils; no recording devices.
safeguards: Participation is optional and anyone may skip a question.
Ask consent before sharing someone else's story.
No stories leave the room without permission.

tasks.brief: Write a 160–340 word decision brief recommending one label printer for a small lending library. Compare both options using supplied facts, include a concrete use scenario, and state a tradeoff. Do not invent specifications or claim certainty where information is missing. Choose presentation order and voice for this user.

materials.need: Print 60 labels each month; acquisition budget is 100 credits.
materials.unknowns: Reliability and print speed have not been measured. All products and prices are fictional.

tasks.brief: Explain file version history to new volunteers digitizing a local archive in 140–320 words. Include one concrete example, the general mechanism, and a limitation. Use only the supplied facts and choose organization and tone for this user.

facts: Version history saves earlier states of a document.
A volunteer can compare an earlier transcription with the current text and restore a mistaken edit.
Version history on one device may be lost if that device fails.
An independently stored backup protects against that failure; version history is not a substitute for a backup.

tasks.brief: Create a self-contained landing page for Neighborhood Sky Night. Explain its purpose, show a concrete participant activity, present the supplied logistics, and include a labeled reservation button. Choose reading order and visual style for this user. Reservations are a local demo: clicking must show a local acknowledgement rather than send data.

materials.name: Neighborhood Sky Night
materials.activity: Use a printed star chart with a volunteer to identify a constellation.
materials.scope: No equipment is required. The event moves to an indoor star-map activity if cloudy.

tasks.brief: Draft a 120–240 word email inviting returning volunteers to a seed-packing session. Include a subject, purpose, concrete description of what a volunteer will do, logistics, and a reply request. Choose organization and voice for this user; do not invent an address or external link.

materials.activity: Count bean seeds into envelopes and label each envelope with its variety.
materials.reply: Ask recipients to reply by Thursday saying whether they can attend.
materials.access: Seated work is available; materials are provided.

tasks.brief: Build a self-contained HTML data story for the tool-lending coordinator using the supplied monthly counts. Include a visible chart, an accessible table with all six counts, a plain-language finding, and a limitation. Show the change in total loans from April to June without implying a causal explanation. Choose the narrative and visual style for this user. Do not use external chart libraries.

materials.limitations: Three months of synthetic counts; no data on weather, membership, repeat borrowers, or unmet demand.

tasks.brief: Write a 170–350 word troubleshooting guide for volunteers using a museum's audio kiosk. Include the general diagnostic approach, a worked symptom path, distinct branches for the two symptoms, and an escalation condition. Use only the supplied safe steps. Choose information order and voice for this user.

no_sound: Check that the headphone plug is fully inserted.
Set the on-screen volume to the middle.
Try the spare headphones if sound is still absent.
frozen_screen: If the screen remains frozen, press the labeled Restart audio button once.
materials.escalation: If the symptom remains after its steps, record the kiosk number and contact the shift lead. Never open the cabinet or unplug cables inside it.

tasks.brief: Create a Markdown outline for exactly four slides teaching a cooperative tabletop game. Use headings Slide 1 through Slide 4, and give each slide display text and speaker notes, totaling 180–380 words. Include the goal, complete turn sequence, one legal example turn, and both end conditions. Choose the teaching order and voice for this user. These are slide contents, not a rendered deck.

materials.setup: Two to four players share a bridge with zero planks, a supply of six planks, and a timer at six turns. No cards or dice are used.
materials.turn: The active player either adds one plank from the supply to the bridge or passes without moving a plank; then the timer decreases by one. Players take turns clockwise.
materials.win: The group wins immediately when the bridge reaches four planks, before decreasing the timer for that turn.
materials.loss: The group loses if the timer reaches zero before the bridge has four planks.
